_comment: MASTER SYLLABUS TEMPLATE — Populated from PDF for Senior 1 Agriculture.

generic_skills: Talk confidently and explain ideas/opinions clearly
Use a range of media to communicate ideas
Predict outcomes and make reasonable decisions
Work with others to generate ideas
Look for patterns and make generalizations
Use mathematics to justify and support decisions
Use technology to create, manipulate, and process information
Use technology to collaborate, communicate, and refine their work
values: Honesty; uphold and defend the truth at all times
Justice and fairness in dealing with others
Integrity; moral uprightness and sound character

topics.core_competency: The learner understands the sector and of the opportunities in agriculture for making a living in Uganda

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: understand the historical background of agriculture in terms of animal herding, the nomadic way of life, food gathering and hunting (k,u)
understand the value of agriculture to human beings and to society as a whole, and the importance of the farm as a production unit (k, u, v)
understand the value of various farming systems and their socioeconomic impact in Uganda (u, k, a,v)
understand the importance of keeping records in agriculture (u, k, a,v)
understand the requirements of a career in agriculture and key principles of the Labour Act on the living conditions of farmworkers (k, u, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners complete a table to compare agriculture and nomadism. (Definition | Information | Examples)

Investigate the value of agriculture to the population as follows: a. Individually, learners write down the names and occupations of about five family members within their local area, indicating how what they do for their income and livelihood directly or indirectly relates to agriculture.
b. In groups, learners collect pictures/labels/ samples and make posters showing the food and other products people get from crops and animals.

In groups, learners research on the different farming systems in Uganda, noting and reporting to the class on; a. the reasons for different systems in different regions b. their socioeconomic impact at local and national levels
In pairs, learners draw a map of Uganda, research on and indicate the areas of crop production and animal production.

In groups, learners prepare and present a role play of a conversation between two farmers, one who recognizes the importance of keeping records and one who does not. Whole class discussions then consider which is likely to be more productive and why.

In groups, learners visit local shops or a market and identify at least six products imported into Uganda. Find out why these commodities are not produced and processed in Uganda and produce a chart or mind-map to explain the findings.

In groups, learners investigate and prepare a presentation on: a. different agricultural careers and the appeal of each b. the working conditions of farm workers in relation to the provision of basic necessities provided within the agricultural sector

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners carrying out the activities and intervene as necessary to ensure that they are on track to achieve learning outcomes.
Listen to group and pair discussions and ask questions to promote critical and creative thinking and to deepen learning of agriculture.
Evaluate quality of learning by assessing products: tables, lists, posters, reports, maps, role plays, charts, mind-maps, and presentations.

practicals.title: Map of Uganda Crop and Animal Production
practicals.description_verbatim: In pairs, learners draw a map of Uganda, research on and indicate the areas of crop production and animal production.

investigative_skills.text_verbatim: Investigate the value of agriculture to the population
investigative_skills.assessment_method: Evaluate quality of learning by assessing products: tables, lists, posters, reports

syllabus_notes.text_verbatim: In the competence-based approach, the 'student' becomes a 'learner'. The Learning Outcomes can only be achieved through active engagement in the learning process rather than simply absorbing knowledge given by the teacher.

topics.core_competency: The learner uses measurement tools, farm tools, equipment, and implements properly and safely in agricultural activities

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: identify tools used on the farm, including garden tools, wood working tools, metal tools, and the basic tools used for fencing, mechanics and other farming activities (k, u)
demonstrate skills of using farm tools and implements correctly for better production(s, a,v)
show skill in using common measurement tools for length, volume, time and mass/weight (k, u,s)
show skills in handling conversion of agricultural measurements into SI units (u, k, s)
demonstrate basic occupational safety and health standards in agriculture(u,s, a,v)
show skills in applying the steps in giving first aid on the farm and during agricultural activities (k, u, s, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In pairs, learners categorise different farm and measurement tools according to their uses in the garden, workshop, animal and crop husbandry, and building. Discuss how each tool is used and prepare a report to present conclusions.
In groups or as a project, learners design and construct low cost tools like a sprayer, rake, mallet, dibber, using locally available materials.
In pairs, learners practice converting different measurements in agriculture into the standard units (SI units)
In groups, learners review the basic occupational safety and health standards that apply to agriculture and develop a procedure for community members to follow.

In groups, learners research on First Aid and the basic occupational safety and health standards in agriculture by listening to an invited speaker or using the Internet or other resources. Present the group’s conclusions about what all agriculture workers should know and be able to do with respect to paying attention to health and safety and carrying out First Aid.
In groups, learners demonstrate to the rest of the class how to use farm tools and equipment safely and how to minimise risk during agricultural activities.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners using tools, equipment, and implements to check whether they are used effectively and safely.
Observe learners carrying out first aid operations and check understanding of key principles and routines with focus on cooperation and collaboration.
Listen to learners’ discussions and intervene to correct misunderstandings and ensure progress towards achievement of learning outcomes.

Evaluate products to gauge learning of groups and individuals: reports on safe and effective use of tools, tool designs and tools constructed, unit conversions, safety procedures, presentations on safety and first aid, demonstrations on safe use of tools.

topics.core_competency: The learner understands how soil is formed from rocks through the process of weathering.

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: show skills in analyzing soil and identifying its different components (s,v)
understand various types of weathering processes and factors influencing soil formation (u, k, s,v)
show skills in distinguishing between the different soil particles, soil textures, and soil structures, as well as soil profile horizons and types of soils as used for agricultural purposes (u, s,v)
show skills in soil sampling (u,s)
understand the importance of plant nutrients and soil pH (u, s,v)
demonstrate soil improvement practices and understand their effects on plant growth (u, s, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: In groups or pairs, learners’ analyses soil composition by means of experiments to determine the presence of organic matter, air, water, mineral salts, and living organisms. Groups report conclusions to the class, relating to the components of soil and techniques used to identify the components.
In groups, learners research and use the different methods of carrying out soil sampling; high light the main steps and reasons why in a report.

In pairs or groups, learners carry out mechanical analysis of soil, analysis by sedimentation and investigations of water holding capacity and drainage and produce reports on the techniques and their findings.
In groups, learners employ a running dictation to discuss and share information about types of weathering that lead to soil formation. Groups produce diagrams to explain how soil is formed.

In groups, learners determine pH of soil samples using a soil testing kit (containing materials like test tubes, indicators, soil samples, droppers, barium sulphate, Munsell chart) and recommend appropriate action to improve soils.
In groups, learners research soil fertility, then dig a soil profile and prepare compost manure for use in a farmer’s garden including how to earn from the activities.
As a class, collaboratively, explore and prepare a report on the main functions of the following plant nutrients: nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe how learners carry out scientific experiments of soil composition, mechanical analysis or sedimentation, soil pH, soil sampling, water holding capacity and drainage to find out if they are making progress towards learning outcomes and intervene to deepen learning.
Listen to pair and group discussions and offer guidance to ensure that all individuals engage and develop skills and understanding.

Evaluate learning through quality of products: reports on soil components and analysis techniques, reports on soil sampling and soil formation diagrams, recommendations for improving soil pH, soil profiles and compost prepared, and reports on effects of NPK on plants.

topics.core_competency: The learner selects a suitable vegetable for a locality and carries out all the processes required in order to grow and market the vegetable

learning_outcomes.outcome_text: know a range of vegetables grown locally and understand their value in both nutritional and financial terms (k,u, a,v)
understand how to select an appropriate vegetable for growing locally (k,, a, v, u)
Establish a nursery and apply good practice for vegetable growing (k, u,s,v)
show skills in preparing bio pesticides and plant derivatives (k, u, s, v)
Handle vegetables during and after harvest in order to maintain quality (s, a,v)
Market vegetables effectively (s, a,v)
Follow food safety guideline for harvested fresh vegetables (u, s, a,v)

suggested_learning_activities.description: Using think-pair-share, learners identify the common vegetables in their locality and discuss the value of vegetables in the diet and as a commodity, presenting conclusions in drawings and/or a written report.

As a class, learners select and use a method of gathering information and design a survey tool to use in collecting data on vegetable growing in the locality. Collect findings in a whole class report.
In groups, learners develop and conduct a survey, including interviews with appropriate groups of people, to collect data on vegetables so as to select one for growing.
As a class, learners develop and document a budget for constructing a nursery bed, procuring materials, establishing a nursery bed, and raising vegetable seedlings.
In pairs or small groups, learners grow, care for and manage vegetables through to maturity.

In groups, learners prepare bio pesticides and plant derivatives from locally available materials like tephrosia, Black Jack, neem tree, tick berry leaves, hot pepper/chili, pawpaw leaves and seeds, and research the uses of each. Apply as appropriate to growing vegetables.
In pairs, learners develop and apply a marketing strategy for their vegetables.
In pairs, learners research on and brainstorm the food safety guidelines for harvested fresh vegetables and design a set of criteria to explain the guidelines to the community.

suggested_assessment_activities.description: Observe learners as they plan and carry out the survey on vegetable growing, focusing on planning activities, how they gather and record information, how they build rapport with respondents and the debrief of each group.

Observe learners establishing a nursery bed, transplanting seedlings, caring for developing plants, harvesting, and marketing of vegetables. Check on skills development, understanding of procedures, safe practice and food safety guidelines including the attitudes exhibited.
Listen to learners’ conversations and offer prompts or ask questions to deepen learning and guide learners towards achievement of learning outcomes.

Evaluate learning through quality of products: drawings/ written reports, survey reports, conclusions about vegetable selection, budget reports; progress of vegetables at each stage of development, preparation of bio pesticides and plant derivatives and their application to plants, marketing strategies, reports on plant nutrients, and their effects.
